traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Easily recognized by its large, round to pear-shaped fruiting body that can reach impressive sizes. The inside (gleba) is initially solid and white, becoming yellowish and finally olive-brown as it matures. When fully mature, the puffball releases its spores through an opening or when the fruiting body is disrupted. This species is edible when young, and the interior flesh is completely white. However, it becomes inedible as it matures and the spores develop, turning the flesh into a mass of olive-brown powder. Always ensure the flesh is pure white throughout before consumption, as other, inedible or toxic puffball species can appear similar when young.
